item.title: Bridging the Semantic Gap in Surface Pollutant Retrieval via Implicit Tensor Alignment of Heterogeneous Satellite Data
item.description: Satellite-based pollutant monitoring is frequently bottlenecked by the resolution-frequency tradeoffs inherent in disparate sensor constellations. While multisensor integration is a potential solution, reconciling the semantic and radiometric discrepancies between heterogeneous platforms remains a fundamental challenge. We propose a cross-sensor alignment framework, implemented via the cross-sensor air-pollutant retrieval network (CSAR-Net). The core innovation is an implicit tensor fusion module (ITFM), which uses shared forward and transposed projections to coordinate complementary representations from heterogeneous sensor streams within a latent feature space. This structural alignment explicitly mitigates spurious correlations with coarse proxies—a pervasive bias, where deep networks over-rely on low-resolution atmospheric signals at the expense of fine-grained spectral fidelity. To ensure cross-regional robustness, a multiobjective optimization strategy is introduced to harmonize retrieval consistency. Extensive validations demonstrate that CSAR-Net reduces root mean square error (RMSE) by 13% relative to the evaluated advanced baselines. Crucially, the framework achieves an $R^{2}$ of 0.88 with only 500 local samples for fine-tuning, confirming its high-sample efficiency and capacity for rapid deployment across disparate metropolitan areas. This work establishes a scalable, methodologically rigorous foundation for high-precision environmental monitoring using multiconstellation satellite data.
item.authors: Zekai Shi;Yaowei Zhang;Meng Zhang;Bo Zhang;Wenting Tang;Haokun Zhang;

item.title: SCEA: Clustering Method for Detecting Hotspots in Irregularly Gridded Spatial Data
item.description: We present a new unsupervised clustering-based algorithm, spatial clustering of elevated-valued areas (SCEA), for detecting and outlining hotspots in spatial datasets with continuous attributes. The method extends the principles of density-based clustering by introducing a value-dependent radius function that adapts locally to the density of the data and the magnitude of the attributes. Unlike many conventional hotspot detection approaches, SCEA does not require the data to be on a regular grid or to have well-defined neighbors, and it remains robust in the presence of missing values, all of which are common characteristics of satellite remote sensing data. We evaluate SCEA’s performance with synthetic datasets, exploring the two main parameters of the algorithm and their relationship to different noise levels. Furthermore, we demonstrate its potential to capture meaningful information with Sentinel-5P TROPOMI satellite observations of tropospheric NO2. The generality of the algorithm and its lack of dependence on training data make SCEA a promising tool for automatic hotspot detection in large-scale remote sensing and other spatial datasets with continuous attributes.
item.authors: Elias Ervelä;Laia Amorós;Amanita Mikkonen;Johanna Tamminen;

item.title: PKGD: Physics Knowledge-Guided Diffusion Model for Underwater Image Enhancement
item.description: Underwater images often suffer from color distortion, low contrast, and blurred details due to light absorption and scattering in water, posing significant challenges to underwater vision tasks. Many deep learning-based methods overlook the complex underwater optical imaging process, thereby reducing interpretability and enhancement performance. In addition, light scattering caused by suspended particles can lead to image blurring, making detail enhancement more difficult. To address the above issues, we propose a novel physics knowledge-guided diffusion (PKGD) model that integrates physical priors into the diffusion process to effectively enhance underwater image quality. Specifically, PKGD consists of high-frequency prior generation (HPG) module, underwater imaging constraint (UIC) module, and physical perception diffusion model (PPDM). The HPG module integrates original features with multiscale high-frequency information to generate physical priors such as background light and transmission maps. The UIC module combines these priors with the underwater imaging model to produce a preliminary enhanced image as an auxiliary map. Finally, the PPDM considers both the background light and the auxiliary image to guide diffusion, generating images with clearer textures and higher quality. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The code is available at https://github.com/Yyh-cc/PKGD.git
item.authors: Lin Shi;Yunhui Yang;Yi Liu;Huibing Wang;Xianping Fu;Guangqi Jiang;

item.title: Bathymetric Reconstruction Using Time-Series Satellite Images and Minimal In Situ Data
item.description: This study proposes a method for reconstructing bathymetric terrain heights using time-series satellite images combined with a bathymetric interpolation technique. Conventional approaches of bathymetric surveys require LiDAR or echo sounders, which require significant cost and time. To overcome this limitation, we propose an algorithm to reconstruct an internal digital elevation model (DEM) of terrains under water bodies. We extract water boundaries from time-series satellite images. The extracted boundaries are treated as contour lines of bathymetric terrain, whose elevation values are not known. The contour lines are used as constraints during a hydrological bathymetric interpolation process. By assigning a true elevation to one water boundary and utilizing elevation values of nearby terrain, we reconstruct a bathymetric DEM. We can estimate a new water level from a new satellite image by overlaying a new water boundary on the bathymetric DEM reconstructed. We can validate the bathymetric DEM by comparing the estimated water level with the reference in situ water level. The proposed method was tested on three reservoirs using high-resolution KOMPSAT-3A images. With one reference water boundary and five nonreference water boundaries, the proposed method achieved an overall mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.61 m using six validation images for each reservoir, with MAEs of 0.61, 0.75, and 0.47 m for Nogok, Maegok, and Pungdo, respectively. These results show that time-series water boundaries can serve as effective constraints for bathymetric reconstruction and water-level estimation in small- and medium-sized reservoirs with limited in situ measurements.
item.authors: Hongjun Youn;Taejung Kim;

item.title: Maize Plant Height Estimation Using UAV and PlanetScope Imagery: A Comparison of 3-D Point Cloud and Machine Learning Approaches
item.description: Plant height (PH) is an essential indicator of crop growth and development, playing a critical role in field management and yield estimation. While recent advancements in remote sensing technologies have improved PH measurement capabilities, existing methods often encounter challenges related to accuracy, spatial resolution, and environmental conditions. In this study, we utilized low-altitude uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery and Planet satellite remote sensing data to explore PH measurement methods based on 3-D reconstructed point clouds and inversion from spectral and texture features. First, a 3-D point cloud method was used to generate a canopy height model (CHM) from a digital surface model (DSM) and a digital terrain model (DTM). Second, this study compared the accuracy of four machine learning methods: eXtreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), random forest (RF), partial least-squares regression (PLSR), and support vector regression (SVR), for PH inversion at the field scale. The results show that the direct 3-D point cloud method is the most accurate for PH estimation, achieving an $R^{2}$ of 0.98. For the machine learning inversion, the fusion of texture and spectral features consistently yielded the best performance for both data sources. Using high-resolution UAV imagery, XGBoost and RF models achieved the highest performance with an $R^{2}$ of 0.74. With 3-m PlanetScope imagery, the XGBoost model was the top performer, reaching a maximum $R^{2}$ of 0.59. On the contrary, the SVR model was consistently outperformed across all scenarios, highlighting the importance of appropriate model selection. Ultimately, high-resolution UAV imagery provided more accurate and reliable data for PH inversion compared to PlanetScope imagery. This study confirms the superiority of direct 3-D measurement and provides a clear guide for feature engineering and model selection in spectral-based PH estimation, providing new directions for future crop monitoring and precision agriculture research.
item.authors: Ke Li;Qing Li;Yanan Wei;Dalei Hao;Weijian Yu;Yelu Zeng;

item.title: From Relation to Structure: Spatial-Semantic Guidance and Structure Refinement Network for Multimodal Remote Sensing Segmentation
item.description: Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in remote sensing image (RSI) interpretation, aiming at pixel-wise classification of land cover. Recently, multimodal RSI semantic segmentation has attracted significant attention for its ability to alleviate the information bottleneck inherent in unimodal methods. However, existing multimodal methods often emphasize feature alignment and complementarity while overlooking the inherent coexistence and mutually exclusive relationships among land covers, frequently resulting in fragmented predictions. Moreover, achieving fine-grained boundary segmentation remains a crucial challenge. To address these challenges, we propose R2SNet, a spatial-semantic guidance and structure refinement network for multimodal RSI segmentation. The core innovation of R2SNet lies in a progressive optimization strategy that guides from semantic relations modeling to spatial structure refinement via three collaborative modules. Specifically, the asymmetric dual-branch (ADB) encoder performs modality-specific extraction of semantic and geometric features to mitigate computational redundancy and modal interference. Subsequently, the spatial-semantic guided cross-modal fusion (SGCF) module explicitly embeds spatial-semantic priors into the fusion process to suppress unreasonable relationships. Finally, the progressive structure refinement (PSR) decoder aggregates multiscale contexts and employs an eight-directional selective scanning mechanism to enhance structural integrity and refine boundaries. Extensive experiments on the ISPRS Vaihingen, ISPRS Potsdam, DDHR, and WHU-OPT synthetic aperture radar (SAR) datasets demonstrate that R2SNet outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, particularly regarding semantic consistency and boundary precision. The code will be available at: https://github.com/bnu-wgy/R2SNet
item.authors: Guangyi Wei;Qianpeng Chong;Zhenxi Wang;Zongyao Yin;Dan Hu;Yinggang Zhang;Xianchuan Yu;

item.title: Adaptive Chirplet Transform and Its Application in Sedimentary Cycle Division
item.description: Sedimentary cycle division serves as a core geological theory for analyzing depositional environments and holds significant guiding importance for reservoir distribution prediction. Time–frequency (TF) analysis is a key technique in this context, and its effectiveness depends on the ability to clearly reveal variations in tuning frequency caused by changes in formation thickness. To improve the energy concentration of TF representations (TFRs), this article proposes an adaptive chirplet transform (ACT) for more accurately characterizing sedimentary cycles. The method first locates the instantaneous frequency (IF) trajectory of each mode within the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) domain using a local maximum criterion. Subsequently, based on the located trajectories, an adaptive chirp-rate estimator (AC) is constructed to accurately capture the frequency-modulation characteristics of each mode. Then, an effective window is defined according to the TF spectral energy distribution theory to delineate the distribution area of TF energy for each mode. Finally, based on the AC, the chirplet transform is adaptively constructed within the effective window corresponding to each mode. The theoretical analysis and synthetic signal experiments demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances the energy concentration of the TFR while maintaining excellent signal reconstruction fidelity. Furthermore, analysis results of ACT on three typical geological models of sedimentary cycles and field seismic data show that this method can effectively identify sedimentary cycle patterns, indicating promising application potential.
item.authors: Peng Chen;Hui Chen;Huailiang Li;Ying Hu;Xuping Chen;Yutao Xie;

item.title: The EAR Radio Frequency Interference Detection and Geolocation Methodology: Application to the NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance Product
item.description: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) (NISAR) mission February 2026 public data release includes 13 803 Level-2 Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance (GCOV) granules reporting measured normalized radar cross sections (NRCSs). An investigation of L-band radio frequency interference (RFI) in the GCOV product is presented that demonstrates the susceptibility of the mission’s observations to anthropogenic transmissions. An “Elliptical ARtifact” (EAR) RFI detection and geolocation methodology is described and applied to NISAR GCOV products. Because GCOVs represent multilooked measurements, existing RFI detection methods that process “raw” in-phase and quadrature backscatter returns are not applicable. The EAR method instead performs detections based on the “shape” of backscatter intensity anomalies consistent with the properties of NISAR’s SweepSAR mode of operation. Results in the vicinity of known sources of interference are used to demonstrate the performance of the EAR method. Larger scale tests further reveal 2396 detections representing more than 500 distinct sources across locations included in the February 2026 public data release. The majority of the sources identified in this “proof of concept” demonstration do not appear to have been previously reported, so the need for RFI detection beyond that available from a priori information on potential RFI sources is emphasized. The use of NISAR’s multiple operational modes in characterizing RFI source properties is also demonstrated. While future NISAR data releases are expected to include additional mission-provided RFI detection and mitigation, the EAR technique will remain useful for independent assessment of mitigation performance and for identifying residual RFI corruption in the NRCS products of NISAR or other SAR missions.
item.authors: Mohammad M. Al-Khaldi;Joel T. Johnson;James Gaudreau;Miranda Holloway;Rajat Bindlish;Jeonghwan Park;Dustin Horton;

item.title: SSDiffNet: Semantic-Guided and Structure-Consistent Diffusion for Aerial Visible-to-Infrared Image Translation
item.description: Visible-to-infrared image translation in aerial scenarios is fundamentally challenged by severe cross-modal appearance discrepancies, complex land-cover semantics, and large variations in brightness distribution. Existing methods, largely developed for natural scenes, often fail to jointly preserve semantic correspondence and fine-grained structural consistency when applied to aerial imagery, leading to semantic misalignment and local structural distortion despite visually plausible global appearance. To address these challenges, we propose SSDiffNet, a diffusion-based framework that explicitly enforces semantic alignment and structural consistency for aerial visible-to-infrared image translation. Instead of relying on global appearance matching, SSDiffNet guides the diffusion process with cross-modal semantic priors while constraining structural stability throughout generation. Specifically, an infrared image adaptive module (IIAM) adapts the diffusion decoder to infrared imaging characteristics under joint spatial- and frequency-domain constraints, enabling more faithful infrared-style reconstruction. A cross-modal semantic feature guidance module (CSFGM) injects learned visible-to-infrared semantic priors into multilevel denoising features, effectively enhancing regional semantic correspondence. In addition, a dual structural consistency constraint module (DSCCM) enforces invariant structural representations under equivalent transformations, substantially reducing structural deviation and local distortion during generation. Extensive experiments conducted on three public aerial visible-to-infrared datasets demonstrate that SSDiffNet consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both visual quality and quantitative metrics.
item.authors: Zhe Guo;Lan Wei;Rui Luo;Jiayi Liu;Shaohui Mei;

item.title: MGSC-Net: Multisemantic Guided Spatial–Frequency Collaborative Network for UAV-Based Infrared and Visible Image Fusion
item.description: Infrared and visible image fusion (IVIF) plays a critical role in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based all-weather aerial perception. However, in aerial scenarios, thermal targets are typically small scaled and easily submerged in complex backgrounds. Existing methods often face a severe feature compromise dilemma: enhancing the saliency of tiny infrared targets tends to oversmooth the vast visible background textures, whereas improving background clarity inevitably attenuates the thermal energy. This phenomenon primarily stems from the incompatibility between isomorphic networks and dual-modal heterogeneous data, where fragile small target signals are easily diluted in the spatial domain. To fundamentally alleviate these issues and achieve a highly robust cross-modal feature expression, this article proposes a multisemantic guided spatial–frequency collaborative network (MGSC-Net). In particular, the network adopts an asymmetric architecture at the encoder, designing a dual-branch extraction mechanism to independently decouple the thermal features of small targets and high-fidelity visible textures. In the fusion stage, a spatial–frequency collaborative strategy is introduced, utilizing frequency-domain priors to accurately anchor tiny targets and adaptively guide the fusion of spatial semantics. In the decoding stage, a progressive cross-scale reconstruction framework and a composite loss function are formulated. Extensive experiments on UAV and common datasets demonstrate that the proposed MGSC-Net achieves superior performance in both subjective and objective evaluations. It establishes an excellent visual balance between tiny targets and complex backgrounds, effectively improving the detection accuracy of downstream UAV vision tasks. The GitHub link is https://github.com/nchuhxn/MGSC-Net
item.authors: Xiaonan He;Yukun Xia;Jianyao Li;Congxuan Zhang;Zhen Chen;

item.title: Knowledge-Infused Temporal Fusion Transformer for Interpretable Riverbank Deformation Forecasting Using Sentinel-1 InSAR Time Series
item.description: Forecasting riverbank deformation requires characterizing complex spatiotemporal heterogeneity governed by coupled hydro-meteorological forcing and site-specific geomorphology. Although deep learning has shown promise for geohazard prediction, existing models for fluvial instability largely operate as black boxes, lacking both physical transparency and spatial transferability. This study proposes the knowledge-infused variational mode decomposition (VMD)-temporal fusion Transformer (TFT), knowledge-infused VMD-TFT (KI-VTFT), a physically constrained and interpretable framework that embeds domain knowledge into data-driven forecasting through two complementary pathways: 1) signal-level priors, injected via Bayesian-optimized VMD (BO-VMD), which partitions displacement into trend, periodic, and residual components; and 2) spatial-level priors, encoded through seven static geomorphic attributes that condition predictions on terrain-controlled susceptibility. The framework was applied to continuous displacement fields derived from 177 Sentinel-1 images (2021–2024) using small baseline subset interferometric synthetic aperture radar (SBAS-InSAR) across three subreaches of the Lower Yangtze River (LYR). At the five-step (60-day) forecasting horizon, KI-VTFT achieved a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 2.29 mm and an R2 of 0.97, reducing RMSE by 25.96%–65.12% relative to gated recurrent units (GRUs), long short-term memory (LSTM), temporal convolutional networks (TCNs), and Transformer baselines. Interpretability analysis revealed that VMD components drove 64.52% of encoder feature importance, while distance to thalweg (22.51%) and elevation (20.78%) dominated the static controls; temporal attention weights peaked during the May–August flood season, consistent with regional hydrological cycles. Independent validation using uncrewed aerial vehicle and uncrewed surface vessel (UAV–USV) bathymetric surveys, acoustic Doppler current profiler (ADCP) flow measurements, and sediment sampling supported the physical plausibility of model-identified drivers. Furthermore, zero-shot transfer to the separate Wuwei Reach maintained an RMSE of 2.77 mm without retraining, outperforming the strongest baseline, the Transformer (3.65 mm), under identical conditions and demonstrating the framework’s potential for cross-reach generalization.
item.authors: Weijie Ding;Heqin Cheng;Zhaocai Wang;Dongping Chen;Junhao Wu;Ruonan Bao;Wenqiu Qu;Irene Cheng;

item.title: Efficient 3-D Imaging Algorithm for Multilayer Dielectrics Based on MIMO-SAR System
item.description: The millimeter-wave (MMW) multiple-input multiple-output synthetic aperture radar (MIMO-SAR) system is highly valued in nondestructive testing due to its high resolution, robust penetration, and multidimensional data acquisition. Nevertheless, most existing imaging techniques are constrained to free-space or half-space scenarios, which typically leads to spatial blurring and low computational efficiency in multilayered dielectric applications. This study addresses these challenges by proposing an accurate and computationally efficient imaging algorithm for multilayered targets. The algorithm is developed based on a scalar Green’s function formulation for multilayer dielectric media, incorporates transverse-wavenumber continuity conditions at the interfaces, and employs spherical wave decomposition for efficient wavefield expansion. By integrating the fast Fourier transform (FFT) with multilayer phase compensation, the method achieves accurate focusing while maintaining high computational efficiency. Simulation and experimental results confirm that the proposed algorithm achieves comparable imaging quality with significantly improved computational efficiency compared with conventional approaches.
item.authors: Xu Chen;Changyu Liu;Yilin Jiang;Bin Deng;Mengxiao Hao;Yu Wang;Muran Guo;

item.title: Model, Source, and Analysis of BiSAR Maritime Moving Target’s Spatial Resolution
item.description: High-resolution imaging of maritime moving targets is of critical importance for maritime domain awareness and defense applications. Bistatic synthetic aperture radar (BiSAR) enables imaging for both stationary scenes and dynamic targets, where spatial resolution serves as a fundamental metric for system design and performance evaluation. While the resolution for static scenes can be derived from platform kinematics, it is invalid for moving targets owing to unknown translational motion and 3-D oscillations. Two fundamental limitations hinder current resolution analysis for moving targets: 1) direct application of such static-scene formulations to moving targets yields inaccurate resolution results, leading to failure of the system design; and 2) the resolution of moving targets depends on numerous factors, necessitating both quantitative and qualitative understanding of its statistical behavior. To address this issue, the resolution model and the physical source of BiSAR maritime moving targets have been systematically established and comprehensively characterized. First, the echo signal model of a maritime moving target in BiSAR is established, and the 2-D spatial resolution model is derived based on the gradient resolution theory. Subsequently, the azimuth resolution contribution index (ARCI) is proposed to quantitatively evaluate the individual contributions of the transmitter, receiver, and target motion to the azimuth resolution. Finally, a comprehensive analysis was carried out to investigate the time-varying characteristics of resolution and ARCI, as well as to analyze the impact of sea states, target rotation parameters, and platform configuration. The validity of the proposed ARCI and the derived theoretical framework is confirmed through numerical simulations.
item.authors: Junjie Wu;Qing Yang;Junyan Li;Zhongyu Li;Qian Liu;Jianyu Yang;

item.title: D2CMFDet: Disparity-Guided Dynamic Cross-Modal Mamba Fusion for Multispectral Object Detection
item.description: Existing multispectral object detectors struggle to balance wide-area cross-modal discrepancy modeling with high-resolution local detail preservation. To address this bottleneck, we propose D2CMFDet, a disparity-guided dynamic fusion framework that integrates learnable state-transition modeling with cross-modal feature calibration. Here, disparity denotes a channelwise feature-response discrepancy between RGB and infrared branches in the learned representation space, rather than geometric or stereo disparity, and it is not an estimate of modality reliability. At its core lies a unified Disparity-Guided Cross-Modal Mamba Fusion (DGCM) engine, which follows a cascaded enhance-then-fuse architecture. Within DGCM, the dynamic feature enhancement module (DFEM) embeds a diagonal local differential convolution (DLDConv), implemented as a structurally modulated convolution with a diagonal bias, to strengthen direction-sensitive local structural cues before global fusion. After this local enhancement stage, the calibrated modality features are converted into a constructed joint feature, which is processed by the Joint-Feature Mamba Fusion (JFMF) module through linear-complexity state-space modeling. This design explicitly separates two roles: DFEM preserves modality-specific local calibration, whereas JFMF performs efficient global modeling on the constructed joint feature. Extensive experiments on public RGBT datasets demonstrate that D2CMFDet achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive performance in detection accuracy, inference speed, and robustness with favorable computational overhead. Code is available at https://github.com/jacksonwu09/D2CMFDet
item.authors: Hai Yang;Xingdu Wu;Chenhai Wei;Yunfei Tong;Dan Zhou;Tianyi Zhou;Ting Xiao;Qian Zhang;Qin Zhou;Zhe Liu;Zhe Wang;

item.title: A Physics-Inspired and Data-Driven Nonlinear Hyperspectral Unmixing Model via a Recursive Interaction Structure
item.description: Hyperspectral unmixing is a fundamental task for fine-grained material characterization, aiming to decompose mixed pixels into pure endmember spectra and their corresponding abundances. However, traditional linear mixing models (LMMs) are inherently limited by neglecting complex nonlinear scattering effects. To address this, existing multilinear models typically rely on physics-driven formulations based on prior knowledge, such as scattering probabilities. In this work, we propose a novel data-driven modeling paradigm with a physics-inspired recursive interaction structure. By explicitly constructing high-order interactions between linear components and latent features through learnable weights at each layer, the model systematically captures composite nonlinearities. Furthermore, a learnable scalar parameter is introduced to dynamically gate the contribution of nonlinear components, significantly enhancing the model’s adaptive representation capability. To implement the proposed model, a concise and efficient dual-stream network architecture is developed. Specifically, the abundance estimation stream integrates multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and attention mechanisms to effectively extract joint spatial–spectral features. Meanwhile, an independent endmember stream is designed to distill pure spectral signatures from a global perspective. Combined with a pretraining strategy, the proposed framework significantly reduces computational complexity while achieving competitive unmixing accuracy, thereby striking a superior balance between performance and efficiency.
item.authors: Zehui Jin;Xiaorui Yi;Hongjuan Zhang;

item.title: CCEM-Net: Conflict-Aware Cross Evidential Modulation for Hyperspectral Change Detection
item.description: Hyperspectral change detection (HSCD) remains challenging due to spectral inconsistency across bitemporal observations, heterogeneous spatial change patterns, and ambiguous decision boundaries that induce predictive uncertainty. Existing methods mainly rely on deterministic representation learning, lacking mechanisms to model uncertainty and resolve such conflicts, often resulting in overconfident and unreliable predictions. To address these issues, we propose CCEM-Net, a conflict-aware evidential deep learning (EDL) framework for reliable HSCD. Specifically, a change-aware interaction (CAI) module is introduced to model cross-temporal dependencies, suppress pseudo-changes, and enhance change-relevant responses via dual gating. A parallel adaptive multiscale spectral and spatial (AMSS) module further captures heterogeneous patterns through temporal-difference-guided multiscale feature aggregation. To handle decision ambiguity, we develop a conflict-aware cross evidential modulation (CCEM) mechanism that models branch predictions as Dirichlet distributions to quantify uncertainty. By measuring interbranch conflict via Jensen–Shannon (JS) divergence, CCEM adaptively modulates evidence strength. Subsequently, reliable decision-level fusion is performed using the Yager rule. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that CCEM-Net consistently achieves the superior performance in both accuracy and reliability compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. The code will be publicly available at: https://github.com/fwx0314/CCEM-Net
item.authors: Shufang Xu;Wenxuan Fei;Shuyu Fei;Runhua Sheng;Hongmin Gao;

item.title: Sparse Tensor Attention for Hyperspectral Unmixing
item.description: Hyperspectral unmixing (HU) is a fundamental task for resolving the mixed pixel problem by decomposing a hyperspectral image (HSI) into constituent endmembers and their corresponding abundances. Although deep-learning-based HU methods have achieved promising performance, most rely on manually designed network architectures that encode spatial–spectral priors only implicitly, limiting their interpretability and ability to model complex spatial–spectral characteristics. To address this limitation, we propose a self-supervised sparse tensor attention (TA) framework for HU, termed STU. The proposed method builds upon the mathematical connection between self-attention and Tucker decomposition and exploits the nonlocal spatial–spectral self-similarity and low-rank structure inherent in HSIs. Specifically, pairwise dependencies among local spatial–spectral cubes are encoded into a sparse tensorized attention core, which is projected through mode-wise low-rank factor matrices to recover the abundance representations. The resulting abundances are constrained to satisfy the abundance nonnegativity and sum-to-one constraints and are subsequently combined with a learnable endmember matrix under the linear mixture model (LMM) to reconstruct the observed HSI. This formulation integrates data-adaptive nonlocal dependency modeling, multilinear low-rank representation, and physically consistent endmember-abundance estimation within a unified framework. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that STU achieves competitive or superior performance compared with representative model-based and deep-learning methods.
item.authors: Jingran Wang;Fengchao Xiong;Zhiyuan Wen;Zhuang Zhao;Jun Zhou;Yuntao Qian;

item.title: Visual-Prompt Bidirectional Interactive Learning for Remote Sensing Infrared and Visible Image Fusion
item.description: Remote sensing infrared and visible image fusion (IVIF) aims to leverage the modality advantages of infrared and visible images to enhance the comprehensiveness and precision of visual representations. However, existing text-guided methods are only constrained by the unidirectional text-to-vision semantic guidance paradigm, where textual description biases directly propagate to fusion results. This may lead to deviations in the fusion outputs, thereby suffering from the loss of original visual information. Therefore, this article proposes a visual-prompt bidirectional interactive learning (VP-BIL) method for remote sensing IVIF. The method constructs a bidirectional semantic alignment mechanism based on visual features and prompt representations generated by the text encoder, enabling efficient cross-modal fusion without requiring accurate text annotations. In particular, a text-visual semantic correlation is first established that ensures both semantic alignment accuracy and the preservation of original visual information. Subsequently, a visual-driven text correction module is designed to dynamically calibrate textual description biases, enhancing the cross-modal semantic alignment between the text and vision. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method effectively overcomes the unidirectional dependence limitation of the text-guided paradigm, outperforming the state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods.
item.authors: Fan Zhao;Yidi Wang;Wenda Zhao;Jiao Li;

item.title: PriorCLIP: Visual-Prior-Guided Vision–Language Model for Remote Sensing Image–Text Retrieval
item.description: Remote sensing image–text retrieval (RSITR) plays a crucial role in remote sensing interpretation, yet remains challenging under both closed-domain and open-domain scenarios due to semantic noise and domain shifts. To address these challenges within a coherent framework, we propose PriorCLIP, a visual-prior-guided vision–language model that organizes closed-domain and open-domain retrieval as two complementary realizations of the same learning principle. PriorCLIP first introduces remote sensing scene knowledge as a visual prior, then uses this prior to adapt image and text representations to the available training regime, and finally regularizes the representations in a discriminative common space. In closed-domain retrieval, this principle is instantiated at the sample level: the spatial progressive attention encoder (S-PAE) constructs an instruction-conditioned belief matrix to reweight visual tokens and suppress noisy regions, while the temporal progressive attention encoder (T-PAE) progressively propagates contextual information to strengthen text representations. In open-domain retrieval, the same principle is extended to representation transfer through a two-stage strategy that first pretrains image and text encoders on large-scale coarse-grained pairs and then performs vision-instruction fine-tuning on fine-grained pairs. A cluster-based symmetric contrastive affiliation loss further exploits scene-category structure to improve intraclass compactness and interclass separation, thereby reducing semantic confusion in the common space. Extensive experiments on RSICD and RSITMD benchmarks demonstrate that PriorCLIP achieves substantial improvements, outperforming existing methods by 4.9% and 4.0% in closed-domain retrieval, and by 7.3% and 9.4% in open-domain retrieval, respectively.
item.authors: Jiancheng Pan;Muyuan Ma;Qing Ma;Cong Bai;Shengyong Chen;

item.title: Hierarchical Bilinear Scattering Transformer for Remote-Sensing Image Scene Classification
item.description: In remote-sensing scene classification (RSSC), persistent challenges such as high interclass similarity and substantial intraclass diversity remain key obstacles to accurate recognition. Although vision Transformer (ViT) has demonstrated outstanding performance, it tends to smooth out high-frequency discriminative details due to the inherent low-frequency preference of self-attention. To alleviate the feature oversmoothing induced by self-attention, we propose a novel hierarchical bilinear scattering Transformer (HBS-Former) that jointly captures local frequency-domain details and global semantic context. First, to alleviate the basis-dependent representation limitations of a single wavelet transform, a dual-stream scattering network is proposed by integrating the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and the dual-tree complex wavelet transform (DTCWT). This design enables stable, direction-aware feature extraction in the frequency domain. Second, a global–local dual-path representation module is elaborately designed to capture long-range contextual information and fine-grained local details via global attention and local convolution branches, which effectively strengthens the complementarity of multigranularity feature representations. Furthermore, a hierarchical bilinear fusion (HBF) mechanism is developed to explicitly model second-order interactions among hierarchical features. By modeling pairwise bilinear interactions across hierarchical features, it produces more discriminative image representations. Extensive experiments on three public benchmarks, namely Aerial Image Dataset (AID), NWPU, and UCM, demonstrate that HBS-Former achieves a favorable tradeoff between classification accuracy and model complexity compared with existing RSSC methods. Code will be available at https://github.com/yizhilanmaodhh/HBS-Former
item.authors: Huihui Dong;Tong Wang;Zongfang Ma;Zhijie Li;Hao Zhu;Wenping Ma;Licheng Jiao;

item.title: Nonuniform Haze Removal via Dual-Domain Complementary Strategy and Cross-Subband Transformer for Remote Sensing Images
item.description: Remote sensing images (RSIs) are frequently contaminated by haze interference, which causes spectral distortion and degradation, hindering subsequent interpretation tasks. Current haze removal restoration faces two key challenges: 1) homogeneous processing strategies applied across frequency components fail to account for their differential sensitivity to haze interference and 2) nonuniform haze interference leads to severe loss of local information in heavily obscured patches. To address this issue, we propose a novel dual-domain complementary strategy (DDCS) for nonuniform haze removal, which decomposes the restoration process into two pathways. In the wavelet domain pathway, we innovatively integrate a transformer with wavelet analysis into a cross-subband transformer (CST). It explicitly separates frequencies, reconstructing structural coherence from low-frequency (LL) bands and restoring fine details via interband attention across high-frequency components. In the spatial domain, we propose haze-aware self-learning (HASL) that performs in-image feature learning and transfer. Without relying on external exemplars, HASL estimates haze concentration, identifies clear regions within the same scene as reference sources, and adaptively transfers their features to heavily degraded patches via a learnable compensation mechanism. These two branches are adaptively fused via a dual-stream aggregation gate (DSAG), enabling complementary restoration. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in terms of both quantitative metrics and visual quality, particularly in recovering spectral fidelity and spatial details.
item.authors: Ruohui Zheng;Libao Zhang;

item.title: Dual-Path Learning Toward Open-Vocabulary Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images
item.description: While the landscape of closed-set oriented object detection has been revolutionized in recent years, extending this success to the instances of unseen categories, the core challenge of open-vocabulary object detection (OVD), remains a formidable hurdle. Prevailing methods often resort to a dedicated student detector to channel the cross-modal knowledge from pretrained vision-language models (VLMs), thereby enabling open-vocabulary generalization. However, these approaches, which primarily manifest as either knowledge distillation or pseudo-labeling frameworks, suffer from a fundamental tradeoff: biased region proposal network (RPN) yields poor recall for target objects, while shared detection head induces catastrophic forgetting of base classes. To overcome these limitations, we propose DPNet, a dedicated end-to-end dual-path network for open-vocabulary oriented object detection in remote sensing scenarios. First, we introduce a parameter-efficient multiscale adapter (MSA) that activates hierarchical features from a frozen vision-language encoder, enabling a category-agnostic network to generate high-quality proposals for target objects with varying scales. Second, a decoupled detection pipeline is formulated for base and target classes. This divide-and-conquer fashion alleviates the inherent optimization conflict, preserving base-class recognition fidelity while effectively learning target concepts. By circumventing the need for a student detector, DPNet offers a more streamlined and efficient architecture. Extensive experiments on two standard remote sensing benchmarks—DIOR and DOTA—validate that our solution achieves competitive performance, significantly outperforming pioneering approaches in both base-class precision and novel-class discovery under zero-shot settings. The source code will be available at https://github.com/yanqingyao1994/DPNet
item.authors: Yanqing Yao;Xiang Yuan;Gong Cheng;

item.title: Spatial–Temporal–Spectral Unified Modeling for Remote Sensing Dense Prediction
item.description: Despite advances in deep learning for remote sensing dense prediction, a unified framework for handling heterogeneous data, multiple tasks, and diverse semantic category sets remains elusive. Concretely, multiple correlated dense prediction tasks (e.g., semantic segmentation and change detection) are often modeled independently, requiring separate networks or task-specific decoder heads. Moreover, the semantic label space is typically fixed during training, so changing the target class subset requires modifying and retraining the prediction head. Here, we introduce the spatial–temporal–spectral unified network (STSUN), a unified framework for remote sensing dense prediction. The model employs metadata-informed unified representations generated via hypernetworks, enabling adaptation to inputs with variable spatial resolutions, temporal lengths, and spectral band configurations. Furthermore, it unifies diverse dense prediction tasks within a single architecture through learnable task embeddings and semantic category embeddings that support multiple class subsets represented during training. Experiments under scenario-level joint training on datasets with diverse spatial–temporal–spectral configurations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for modeling multiple dense prediction tasks and semantic class subsets within a single model.
item.authors: Sijie Zhao;Feng Liu;Xueliang Zhang;Hao Chen;Pengfeng Xiao;Junjue Wang;Weihao Xuan;Naoto Yokoya;Lei Bai;

item.title: Beyond Text: Bridging Speech and Satellite Imagery for Efficient Visual Grounding
item.description: While remote sensing visual grounding (RSVG) has emerged as a crucial bridge for human–machine interaction in Earth observation, existing methods rely exclusively on textual queries. In time-critical applications such as disaster rescue and emergency response, this reliance restricts hands-free operation and strips away vital prosodic cues like tone and emphasis, which are highly effective for disambiguating complex geospatial targets. To overcome these limitations, we formally introduce the task of audio-driven RSVG (Audio-RSVG) and construct Audio-detectIon in optical remote sensing (DIOR), a large-scale dataset simulating real-world acoustic environments with diverse timbres and background noise conditions. Furthermore, we propose RSTalker, a robust end-to-end framework designed to directly align speech signals with aerial imagery. By bypassing cascaded automatic speech recognition (ASR) pipelines, RSTalker prevents transcription error propagation, particularly regarding remote sensing terminology. This approach also effectively exploits rich acoustic semantics that are often lost during intermediate text generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RSTalker achieves state-of-the-art localization accuracy and noise robustness. Notably, by eliminating manual data entry and heavy decoder stacks, the proposed paradigm delivers a $3.5\times $ speedup in complete interaction-to-inference time compared to conventional text-based baselines. This paves the way for intuitive, hands-free interaction in urgent remote sensing tasks.
item.authors: Yaoyong Liu;Yue Zhou;Xue Yang;

item.title: U-Net-Accelerated Indirect Boundary Element Method for Efficient Seismic Basin Amplification Simulation
item.description: The indirect boundary element method (IBEM) based on layered half-space Green’s functions (HSGFs) is a powerful tool for parametric studies of basin amplification effects. Once the HSGF is computed for a given basin model, simulating different source configurations can be accomplished in minutes. However, even a one-time calculation of the HSGF for layered media could remain a significant bottleneck, as closed-form solutions are usually unavailable and numerical evaluation is required. This study presents a deep-learning (DL)-assisted IBEM scheme that accelerates HSGF computation through supervised interpolation. We organize the space–frequency domain HSGF as fourth-order tensors indexed by wavefield component, source position, receiver position, and frequency, with source and receiver indices structured according to the basin’s discretization geometry, thereby recasting a significant fraction of the computation as a structured interpolation problem. The dense HSGF sampling intrinsic to IBEM provides abundant self-consistent data, eliminating the need for external training. A case-specific U-Net architecture is trained on a downsampled subset of fully computed HSGFs and then applied to predict the remaining entries. This problem-specific strategy maximizes utilization of IBEM-generated data while circumventing the generalization challenges that limit many learning-based forward solvers. Validation tests on ellipsoidal basin models show that the hybrid scheme achieves over 99% accuracy compared with full-computation References while reducing the overall computation time by approximately 35%–55% depending on the mask rate, corresponding to a saving of about one to two days in the present examples. This methodology could be extended naturally to other basin geometries and boundary integral formulations, and holds promise for large-scale applications in seismic hazard assessment and ground motion simulation.
item.authors: Zhonghan Liu;Zhenning Ba;Siwei Yu;Jingxuan Zhao;Zhili Wei;Hao Hu;

item.title: High-Resolution Migration With Stable SVD-Based Inverse Hessian Compensation
item.description: Conventional Kirchhoff migration is commonly affected by limited resolution, reflector broadening, and sidelobe contamination. Here, we propose DSVD-IHCM, a migration-imaging method that uses singular-value decomposition-based damped inverse Hessian compensation. The method first constructs local point-spread functions (PSFs) from the migration responses of scattering points and then explicitly forms an image-domain Hessian by spatial interpolation. A stable inverse Hessian operator is then constructed by applying damping to the singular-value inverse and is applied to the conventional migration image to reduce blurring and improve resolution. To avoid the memory and computational burden associated with explicit storage and global inversion of the full Hessian, we use blockwise construction, blockwise inversion, and weighted stitching. Experiments with a horizontally layered model, the Marmousi model, and field seismic data show that the constructed Hessian captures the Kirchhoff migration response. Compared with conventional migration and gradient-based image-domain least-squares methods, DSVD-IHCM more effectively compresses the main lobe, suppresses sidelobes and artifacts, and improves reflector focusing and spatial resolution. The method also remains stable and robust for noisy data, providing a practical route to high-resolution image-domain migration compensation.
item.authors: Liwei Song;Yilin Bai;Ying Shi;Ning Wang;

item.title: Toward Practical and Reliable Electromagnetic Inversion: A Semi-Stochastic Lévy Gradient Descent Approach With Trajectory-Based Model Assessment
item.description: Quantitative assessment of inverted models has long been a major challenge in geophysical inversion, particularly in 3-D electromagnetic (EM) inversion. Traditional gradient-based inversion methods are computationally efficient, but their results strongly depend on the initial model and may converge to local minima. Moreover, they generally provide only a global measure of data misfit, such as the rms, rather than spatially resolved information on the reliability of the recovered model. In contrast, fully stochastic methods can deliver uncertainty estimates through posterior probability distributions, yet their computational cost remains prohibitive for 3-D EM inversion. To bridge this gap, we propose a semi-stochastic inversion algorithm based on the Lévy flight process—Lévy Gradient Descent (LGD). This method utilizes gradient information to guide the search direction and employs the Lévy flight process to generate stochastic step sizes, combining gradient-guided local search with broader stochastic exploration of the parameter space. This enables a more comprehensive and efficient exploration of the solution space. More importantly, the statistical information provided by LGD effectively offers assessments for the inversion results, serving as a crucial complementary metric beyond data misfit for interpreting inverted models. This allows for a relative assessment of the structural stability of individual model parameters in the model. We tested the LGD algorithm on both synthetic and real data. The results demonstrate that LGD produces results comparable or superior to nonlinear conjugate gradient (NLCG), while the trajectory-based structural stability indicator offers valuable insights for interpretation. Our new resistivity model of the Yellowstone hotspot region reveals a deep mantle plume head that appears to connect to shallow structures only through weak, moderately conductive channels—suggesting a waning hotspot.
item.authors: Ziyu Tang;Bo Yang;Yi Zhang;
